paper.title_en: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
paper.abstract_en: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.
